plan.G: After research closes, review each candidate together with its correctness results and measurements. Select by the official geometric-mean kernel time across N=4096, 8192, and 16384; do not assume individually measured gains will add. Reuse slower-trial ideas or bases only when useful, and compile and check every combined program afresh. Independently confirm final G using the prescribed protocol, retain the best independently confirmed valid program, and do not restart research.
plan.analysis: I choose N=3: the baseline exposes three complementary opportunities—reuse source-particle data across targets, reuse each loaded source across multiple target outputs, and reduce per-interaction arithmetic. The supplied kernel assigns one target to each thread and serially loops over all sources; it evaluates sqrtf and forms a mass_i-scaled force before dividing by mass_i. These suggest opportunities, but the measurements do not establish which is dominant. The only automatic result is a valid, correct baseline with three listed timings of 1.856535–1.856696 ms and a recorded mean of 1.856629 ms; there are no per-size results or candidate comparisons to support a speedup claim. Keep the exact Particle layout and entry point, one-kernel interface, softening, update order, exact mass preservation, and all-input correctness, including self-interaction exclusion, coincident positions, negative or zero dt, and the extreme-mass case. Test all stated sizes and the independent oracle; no test-specific specialization or fast-math option. Launch-configuration tuning belongs within each relevant algorithm rather than in a separate generic tree, since it is coupled to each mapping.

children.objective: Shared-memory source tiling, one target per thread
children.subject: Explore staging source positions and mass in shared memory in source chunks so multiple target threads reuse each staged source. Keep the output mapping at one target per thread to distinguish this from register-blocked output work. Tune a valid block/items_per_block/shared_memory_bytes configuration and the shared tile layout; handle partial source and target tiles without letting inactive threads skip required barriers. Preserve i==j exclusion, the exact interface and all correctness requirements. Compare using the prescribed three-size geometric-mean kernel-time objective, and retain only candidates that pass the full correctness checks.

Explore assigning a small batch of target particles to each thread, with separate accumulators, so a source particle's loaded position and mass can be reused across those targets. This is an output-axis/register-reuse investigation, not merely another one-target-per-thread shared-memory tile. Tune the batch size and allowed launch configuration while monitoring register pressure and available parallelism. Cover all target tails and preserve the full state, self exclusion, numerical requirements, and exact masses. Measure against the prescribed objective and validate every candidate with the complete oracle/check suite.

Explore lowering the cost of pair evaluation while retaining the one-target-per-thread mapping as a clear comparison: for example, algebraically cancel target mass in the acceleration expression and evaluate inverse distance with rsqrtf to form an inverse-cube factor. Test arithmetic ordering and only consider FMA or loop unrolling when measurements justify them. These transformations change floating-point rounding: preserve softening and self exclusion, use no global fast-math option, and reject any candidate that fails tolerances, oracle checks, or the nonfinite-output constraint, including extreme-mass and coincident-position cases. Compare on the official geometric-mean metric.

decision.rationale: Use measured-correct T1 as the source base and adapt only T2's two-target-per-thread idea: retain T1's shared source tiles, but let each thread maintain separate accumulators for two adjacent target rows. Use block=128, items_per_block=256, and shared_memory_bytes=2048 (four arrays of 128 floats); each staged source is then reused for both target interactions. Preserve ascending source order for each target, independent tail guards and self-exclusion, and ensure all threads reach both barriers. T2 alone was valid but slower (0.002605 s, score 0.416) than T1 (0.001008 s, score 0.648), so its idea is an unverified complement, not a measured gain. Compile, check, and measure this combined candidate afresh; do not infer additive performance.

model_interpretation.claim: Staging each source tile's x, y, z, and mass once per block in shared memory may let the block's target threads reuse those values while retaining one target per thread. Two block-wide barriers protect tile loading and reuse; inactive target lanes still reach both barriers. The source traversal and per-target accumulation order remain unchanged, but no speedup is assumed before measurement.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/launch.json","src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Stage source x, y, z, and mass into four dynamic shared-memory arrays per block, loading one source per lane per tile.","Keep one target particle per thread and preserve the original serial source accumulation order and self-interaction exclusion.","Use unconditional block barriers before reading each tile and before overwriting it; inactive target lanes do not return early.","Configure 256 threads per block and 4096 bytes of dynamic shared memory."]}

model_interpretation.claim: Assigning two adjacent target particles to each thread should reuse each source particle's position and mass across both target interactions, reducing source-load work while retaining each target's original accumulation order.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/launch.json","src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Map each thread to two adjacent output particles and keep separate force accumulators for each.","Load each source particle's position and mass once per source-loop iteration, then reuse them for both target interactions.","Use 128 threads per block while keeping 256 output items per block; guard the second target for odd-sized tails."]}

model_interpretation.claim: For each non-self interaction, rsqrtf plus an inverse-distance cube can replace sqrtf and the distance-denominator division. Since G is 1 and target mass factors out of the summed force before the per-target division, accumulating acceleration directly also removes that target-mass multiplication per interaction and the final division. This changes floating-point rounding, so correctness and speed remain for the controller to establish.
model_interpretation.transformations: {"files":["src/nbody_kernel.cu"],"retained":["Use rsqrtf(distSq) and its cube to form the softened inverse-distance factor instead of sqrtf and division by distSq * dist.","Accumulate acceleration directly after factoring out target mass and G=1, removing the target-mass multiplication from each interaction and the per-target force division."]}
